data.summary: This 8‑week plan uses the two available live classes to anchor the schedule, then builds on each unit with focused practice and timed drills. Each week is capped at 6 hours, and the final week is devoted to mixed review and timed practice to simulate exam conditions.

weeks.focus: Master basic kinematics and free‑body diagram fundamentals.
tasks: Do 15 free‑body diagram problems on 2.2 and self‑grade using the rubric.

weeks.focus: Deepen understanding of motion and Newton’s laws.
tasks: Solve 20 problems on 1.3 and 1.4, then compare solutions with a peer.
Complete 10 Newton’s 2nd law word problems (2.5) and check answers with the scoring guide.

weeks.focus: Apply work, energy, and conservation principles.
tasks: Do 12 work‑energy problems (3.1, 3.4) and annotate each step.
Solve 10 collision scenarios (4.3, 4.4) and write a brief explanation of conservation reasoning.
Do 8 torque calculations (5.3) and verify with a calculator.

weeks.focus: Link rotational energy and angular momentum.
tasks: Solve 10 problems on rotational kinetic energy (6.1).
Work through 5 angular momentum conservation problems (6.3, 6.4).

weeks.focus: Study simple harmonic motion and fluid concepts.
tasks: Answer 5 fluid density questions (8.1) and 5 pressure problems (8.2).
Take a 60‑minute timed practice test covering all units. Afterward, review incorrect answers and summarize key concepts.

data.final_week_advice: Use the final week to simulate exam conditions: complete a full-length timed test, then review mistakes in detail, reinforcing any weak spots before the exam.
